issue.title: Reflect broader range of check constraints for SQLite.
issue.body:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your proposed changes in the Title field above -->

### Description
<!-- Describe your changes in detail -->

These changes are an extended and corrected version of PR https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/pull/11678, which was made by one of our job students and may be closed.
This fixes issue https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/11677.

We've adjusted the check constraint pattern to match a broader range of check constraints that can be encountered.
This includes:
* allowing spaces and special characters in the name of the check constraints.
   This is done as long as none of the SQLite's table constraints keywords are encountered seperated by spaces.
   This prevents the pattern from matching subsequent constraints as part of the name.
* allowing newline, tab or space characters in the constraint definition.

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

I encountered problems noted in #11832, but I found a case not handled by the fix.

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, inspect, CheckConstraint, MetaData
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from typing import Optional


METADATA = MetaData()

class BaseModel(DeclarativeBase):
    metadata = METADATA

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


class Example(BaseModel):
    __tablename__ = 'example'
    value: Mapped[Optional[str]] = mapped_column(doc="Name of the HTML body template.")
    value_2: Mapped[Optional[str]] = mapped_column(
        CheckConstraint('value_2 IS NULL OR value IS NOT NULL',
                        name='value_2_check'))

    next_value: Mapped[str]


# Create an in-memory SQLite database and create the table
engine = create_engine('sqlite:////tmp/test.db')
BaseModel.metadata.create_all(engine)

inspector = inspect(engine)
print(inspector.get_check_constraints("example"))
# 2.0.32 correct
# [{'sqltext': 'value_2 IS NULL OR value IS NOT NULL', 'name': 'value_2_check'}]
# 2.0.33, 2.0.34 incorrect
# [{'sqltext': 'value_2 IS NULL OR value IS NOT NULL), \n\tnext_value VARCHAR NOT NULL, \n\tid INTEGER NOT NULL, \n\tPRIMARY KEY (id', 'name': 'value_2_check'}]
```

Schema from the sqlite:
```
CREATE TABLE example (
	value VARCHAR,
	value_2 VARCHAR CONSTRAINT value_2_check CHECK (value_2 IS NULL OR value IS NOT NULL),
	next_value VARCHAR NOT NULL,
	id INTEGER NOT NULL,
	PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
```

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_
